implementation_notes: Ruby's core has no Future, but Thread covers the pattern with one object: Thread.new { work } starts the call and returns the thread handle immediately, and Thread#value is the collect step - it joins the thread and returns the block's value, re-raising in the caller any exception the block raised, which is exactly the pattern's deferred failure channel. The classic AsyncResult/AsyncCallback structure is therefore rarely written: the handle and the collector collapse, and a callback is just a call made at the end of the block (on the worker thread, with the same affinity caveat as every other language). Thread::Queue and SizedQueue hand results between threads without shared state, and Thread#join without value is the fire-and-forget bookkeeping. The MRI global VM lock means threads overlap I/O but do not run CPU-bound Ruby in parallel (processes or Ractors do), and the gem concurrent-ruby supplies the richer handle/callback shape (Concurrent::Future, Promises) when the platform's thread primitives are too raw.
code_sketch:
pending = Thread.new { fetch_report(id) }     # returns immediately
pending.report_on_exception = true
# caller does other work ...
begin
  report = pending.value                      # collect; re-raises the block's exception
rescue StandardError => e
  warn "async call failed: #{e.message}"
end
pitfalls: An exception raised in a thread is stored, not propagated, until join/value is called: a thread that nobody collects fails silently (Thread.report_on_exception exists to make that visible).
When the main thread exits, all other threads are killed - a background call dies with the program unless it is joined or the process waits for it.
The GVL allows only one thread to execute Ruby at a time: CPU-bound work gains nothing from Thread and needs processes (or Ractors).
One Thread.new per request means one native thread per call; the pattern's scalability argument requires capping concurrency with a pool or a SizedQueue.
Thread#value blocks: calling it on a hot path is a synchronous call with extra steps, and thread-local state of the worker is not the caller's.
